issues.issue: The three Systems granted here — "Accelerated Recovery Performance Protocols," "In Balance Muscle Testing Protocols" and "Wave Site Protocols" — do not match the Systems defined in Section 1.1 and the recital (Accelerated Recovery Program Protocols, Ultra Fit Athletic Mastery Protocols, In Balance Muscle Testing Protocols). What is actually licensed cannot be fixed without reconciling the grant with the definition.

The right to operate "under the business name of 'ARP Wave Clinic'" conflicts with Section 1.3, which states that Licensee "is granted no right, title or license to, or interest in, any ARP Trademarks." The instrument both grants and withholds the right to trade under the ARP name.

Rights are said to be "forfeitable in the event of certain circumstances or occurrences as herein set forth" without identifying which circumstances, and the contract states forfeiture triggers in at least two different places (Section 6.3 and Section 7.1). The phrase "certain circumstances" has no ascertainable content on its face.

Licensor's release on assignment is conditioned on Licensee being "afforded notice of such assignment," while paragraph 14 of the Lease permits Lessor to assign all of its rights "without notice to the Lessee." On an assignment of the combined instrument the notice condition is both required and dispensed with.

The support promised — "Monthly seminars in Minneapolis, Minnesota, Telephone Consultation and Email Support" — is unquantified as to frequency, duration or responsiveness, unlike the prior ARP agreements which specified hours of consultation per month. What Licensor must deliver for the $1,400 monthly fee covering "consultation" is therefore indeterminate.

"An ARP Wave Clinic must exclusively use the Systems ... and must not perform any other type of physical therapy, training or rehabilitative service" does not say whether the restriction binds only the named clinic facility or the Licensee's other businesses and personnel. Its overlap with the separate non-compete in Section 4.6, which is limited to a Territory, makes the reach of the exclusivity contestable.

Performance is measured against "any reasonable guidelines issued by ARP Wave," guidelines that are neither attached nor defined and that Licensor may issue unilaterally at any time. What conduct "reflects favorably" on ARP Wave is likewise given no standard.

"Appropriate technical and organizational measures" to protect patient data is stated without any benchmark, standard or reference to a specific law. Compliance can only be judged against an undefined notion of appropriateness.

This paragraph forbids Licensee to "display ot otherwise make available the System(s) to any other patty without the written consent of Licensor," which cannot be squared with Section 1.2's definition of an ARP Wave Clinic as delivering the Systems' services "to the public" and with Section 4.1's requirement that trained personnel be taught the Systems. It also, unlike the 2010 agreement, omits any express duty to keep the Systems confidential, leaving Section 11.3's survival of "confidentiality and non-disclosure provisions" with little to attach to.

The restraint runs to "any similar or competitive system or Licensee within the Territory defined in the Exclusive Licensee Agreement executed by the parties," but no Exclusive Licensee Agreement is part of this instrument and no Territory is defined anywhere in it. The phrase "or Licensee" is also garbled, so the class of prohibited activity and its geographic scope are both indeterminate.

The clause incorporates the terms of an outside "Exclusive Licensee Agreement," which cannot be squared with Section 8's statement that "This Agreement and exhibits thereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties regarding the subject matter hereof." Whether an unattached agreement can supply the Territory turns on that integration clause.

The $1,400 monthly license fee duplicates Block D of the schedule and the Rent paragraph's "PROTOCOLS $16,800.00," and Section 5 states no duration or end date for the obligation. Whether one or two $1,400 monthly obligations exist, and for how long they run, is unresolved between these provisions.

The term sentence is incomplete: "shall become effective on ___ and shall be continue in full force and effect until ___ unless otherwise terminated," with both dates left blank and a grammatical error in the verb. Neither the commencement nor the expiration of the License can be determined from the words used.

With its own dates blank, the License's duration must be taken from elsewhere — the Lease's "ONE YEAR"/12-month original term and Block A's start date — yet the License is terminable only by Licensor and has no renewal mechanism like the 2010 agreement's annual renewal option. Whether the License expired with the one-year lease or ran indefinitely is a whole-instrument question.

Survival of all covenants "except those covenants as pertaining to future payments to be made by Licensee" cannot be squared with Section 7.1(a)-(b), which on default lets Licensor accelerate "the entire amount owed" and sue for fees "thereafter accruing," or with the Lease's unconditional-payment paragraph. Whether post-termination payment obligations survive is answered both ways.

Automatic termination on any attempted transfer cannot be squared with Section 2.3, which makes such an attempt merely "a breach of this Agreement," and with Section 7.1(e), which gives Licensor an elective remedy to terminate. Whether the license ends by operation of the clause or only upon Licensor's election is left open.

Remedy (c) permits Licensor to "take possession of any or all tangible System(s) ... without any court order," but "System(s)" is defined as protocols, marks and other intellectual property, and the tangible equipment is governed by the separate Lease repossession remedy. What may be seized under this clause is undefined.

Venue is limited to "the Hennepin County, Minnesota, Federal or State District Court" and only "for the enforcement of this Agreement," leaving open whether tort, trade secret or non-compete claims are covered and which federal court is meant. The identical clause in paragraph 21 of the Lease raises the same question for the same dispute.

"This Agreement and exhibits thereto, constitutes the entire agreement" conflicts with paragraph 18 of the Lease, which declares that Lease the entire agreement, and with Sections 4.6 and 7.1, which invoke an Exclusive Licensee Agreement and "any other agreement entered into between Licensor and Licensee." What documents make up the parties' contract — including the earlier 2010 and 2012 ARP agreements — cannot be answered from this clause alone.

Notices must be "sent facsimile transmission or overnight courier," while paragraph 22 of the Lease requires personal delivery, prepaid telegram, or first class/registered/certified mail. The two notice clauses in the same instrument prescribe different and non-overlapping methods for the same parties.

The carve-out for "THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES, IF ANY, MADE IN THE ARP WAVE LEASE AND LICENSE AGREEMENT" leaves open whether the Lease's Warranty paragraph (free repair of defects) is preserved as to the equipment supplied with the Systems. The disclaimer and that repair promise must be read together to know what warranty survives.

The bar on consequential damages sits against paragraph 6 of the Lease, which caps Lessor's liability at rent paid rather than excluding categories of damages, so two different limitation regimes govern one transaction. The savings language "EVEN IF ANY EXCLUSIVE REMEDY PROVIDED FOR HEREIN FAILS OF ITS ESSENTIAL PURPOSE" also refers to an exclusive remedy that the Agreement never designates.

The paragraph waives all claims "except for any breach or breaches of Licensor's contractual obligations," then in the next sentence waives "all rights at law and equity to claim fraud, inaccuracy, imperfection of the System(s)" — leaving unclear whether misrepresentation claims tied to Licensor's contractual promises survive the exception. The two sentences pull in opposite directions on the same claim.

Licensor's disclaimer of any representation as to the "legitimacy, legality [or] non-infringing nature" of the Systems sits against Section 4.4, which puts all regulatory compliance on Licensee, and Section 4.1, which conditions clinic operation on licensed medical personnel. Whether Licensor bears any responsibility for the lawfulness of the licensed practice is only answerable from the instrument as a whole.

This indemnity, limited to third-party claims arising from Licensee's acts, omissions, breach or misrepresentations, overlaps with paragraph 12 of the Lease, which indemnifies Lessor for "any and all claims ... resulting from the equipment" regardless of fault. Which standard governs a claim arising from use of the equipment under the licensed protocols is unresolved.

"Fails to assume in a timely manner" the defense is not defined and no notice period or deadline is fixed anywhere in Section 10.6. When ARP may take over the defense at Licensee's expense therefore has no measurable trigger.

"Any rights herein set forth shall be deemed to be automatically revoked and automatically reassigned to Licensor" does not say whose rights, and read literally would sweep in the Licensee's rights that were never assigned from Licensor as well as any rights of Licensor. "Reassigned" also presupposes an assignment that Section 2.5 says never occurs.

The duty to "immediately return ... all copies or renditions or enhancements of all System(s)" is stated for property that is largely intangible protocols and know-how, so what must be returned, and whether the leased equipment falls within it alongside the Lease's Surrender paragraph, is unclear.

This clause preserves "all confidentiality and non-disclosure provisions of this Agreement," but the Agreement contains no provision so labelled — Section 4.5 imposes only a restriction on making the Systems available to third parties, and the express confidentiality covenant found in the 2010 ARP agreement was dropped. Identifying what survives requires reading the whole instrument.

The disclaimer that the Agreement creates no "franchise" or agency relationship sits against operative terms that license a trade name (Section 2.2), impose a recurring fee (Section 5), and give Licensor control over personnel, training and operations (Section 4). Whether the label controls the substance of the relationship is a whole-contract question.

The guaranty covers "all indebtedness and liability which Lessee/Licensee may have to Lessor/Licensor under this Lease Agreement," naming only the Lease although the instrument comprises both a Lease and a License with separate fee obligations. Whether license fees and non-compete damages are guaranteed turns on that limiting phrase, and the guarantor is left unidentified.
